HOW TO READ THIS ATLAS

The evidence, with its limits.

This first map displays documented well records. It does not estimate the probability that a new well will produce water.

What the colors mean

Positive yield: a source reports production above zero. A historical test is not a promise of sustainable supply.

Dry: a source explicitly documents a dry outcome. Missing yield and zero values alone are not classified as dry.

Plugged / abandoned: a reported closure or abandonment. This does not by itself mean the well was dry. Closure takes precedence in the marker color; earlier yield and dry evidence are preserved in the record.

Unknown: the record does not establish one of those outcomes.

What a record cannot tell you

Water availability changes over time. Records can have approximate coordinates, incomplete tests, and missing depth or quality data.

Potability is not established by a yield measurement. Water chemistry, treatment needs, sustainable pumping, and drilling permissions need separate evaluation.

Dry holes are incompletely reported, so the fraction with positive yields is not a drilling success rate. Different source records may refer to the same physical well.

Study area & measurements

Texas records only. The study circle crosses into Mexico; missing records there do not imply an absence of groundwater. The center is Terlingua Ghost Town.

Records are selected within 50 straight-line miles of Terlingua at 29.3216° N, 103.6160° W. The circle is a geographic filter, not an aquifer boundary.

Depth and water level are reported in feet; production is in gallons per minute. A blank means unavailable, never zero. The median uses water-well records with reported positive depth in the selected site scope, excluding separate plugging reports. Physical wells may appear in more than one source.

Location comparisons use straight-line distances to recorded coordinates. Nearby wells can intersect different fractures, formations, and water quality.
